items.headline: High Surf Advisory issued November 15 at 12:07PM PST until November 16 at 10:00AM PST by NWS Portland OR
items.description:
* WHAT...Large waves and hazardous surf conditions. Breakers up to
25 to 30 feet.

* WHERE...North and Central Coast of Oregon, and South
Washington Coast.

* WHEN...Until 10 AM PST Monday.

* IMPACTS...Destructive waves may wash over beaches, jetties,
and other structures unexpectedly. People can be swept off
rocks and jetties and drown while observing high surf. Minor
beach erosion may damage coastal properties and buildings.
Higher than normal water run-up is expected on beaches and low-
lying shoreline.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The threat of sneaker waves is extreme
during these scenarios. Sneaker waves can suddenly knock
people off of their feet and quickly pull them into the frigid
ocean which may lead to serious injury or drowning.
items.instruction:
A High Surf Advisory means that high surf will affect beaches,
producing rip currents, sneaker waves and beach erosion. Stay
well back from the water's edge and be alert for exceptionally
high waves.

Keep away from large logs on the beach. Water running up on the
beach can easily lift or roll logs which can injure or kill
someone caught in their path.

items.headline: Hazardous Seas Warning issued November 15 at 12:24PM PST until November 16 at 10:00PM PST by NWS Portland OR
items.description:
* WHAT...Very steep and hazardous seas 18 to 23 ft at 16 seconds
and southwest winds 10 to 20 kt with gusts up to 25 kt.

* WHERE...Coastal Waters from Cape Shoalwater to Florence out 60
NM.

* WHEN...Until 10 PM PST Monday.

* IMPACTS...Very steep and hazardous seas could capsize or cause
damage to vessels.
items.instruction:
A Hazardous Seas Warning means hazardous sea conditions are
imminent or occurring. Recreational boaters should remain in
port, or take shelter until waves subside.  Commercial vessels
should prepare for rough seas and consider remaining in port or
taking shelter in port until hazardous seas subside.
